source_evidence.excerpt: Pixel Flipping measures the drop of the respective class logit ... We report the area under the curve (AUC) of this drop at 5% and 20%, where a faster drop means higher area under the drop curve.
PF_p is the trapezoidal area over the first p% of this flipping curve ... Lower is better. The curve tracks the remaining class score.

findings.issue: The chapter preamble at line 9 explicitly distinguishes PF^drop_5/PF^drop_20 (score-drop AUC, higher is better) from PF_5/PF_20 (remaining-logit AUC, lower is better). Later prose calls both simply Pixel Flipping/AUC: line 21 labels the split result AUC@5/AUC@20, line 23 compares Pixel Flipping performance, and lines 55-56 introduce the game study's PF_5/PF_20 as Pixel Flipping area without saying remaining-logit. A reader can mistakenly infer that the reported quantities or their direction are interchangeable.
findings.targeted_action: Add the existing short qualifiers 'score-drop' to the split-study references and 'remaining-logit' to the game-study definition/reference, or use the already introduced PF^drop and PF notation. Preserve the distinct definitions, step sizes, and directions; do not merge or numerically compare these AUCs as one metric.
findings.semantic_status: The values are genuinely different quantities and must remain distinct.

For example, SplitCAM achieves the highest Pointing Game score 0.938 with alpha = 0.4 ... SplitCAM outperforms classical methods on Selectivity, with comparable Pixel Flipping performance as the most faithful baseline LayerCAM. SplitLRP slightly outperforms classical gamma-LRP in localization while staying competitive in Faithfulness.
original_wording_review.thesis_excerpt: On VGG-16, the split methods demonstrate superior performance compared to all considered baselines across the Quantus metric categories. SplitCAM achieves the highest Pointing Game score of 0.938 ... SplitCAM outperforms the classical methods on Selectivity, with Pixel Flipping performance comparable to the most faithful baseline, LayerCAM. SplitLRP slightly outperforms classical gamma-LRP in localization while staying competitive in faithfulness.
original_wording_review.assessment: This is a close sentence-by-sentence paraphrase of the source results, with changes largely limited to architecture spelling, grammar, punctuation and styling. It is the clearest opportunity to retain the source formulation verbatim while updating only cross-reference handling and house spelling. The metric definitions and reported numbers do not need rewriting.

original_wording_review.source_excerpt: Mid-layer SplitCAM shares key visual characteristics with classical gamma-LRP from earlier layers. Compared to standard LayerCAM on the same layer it focuses more weight to all object pixels, while still marking the key object features as especially important. For alpha much less than 0.5, SplitGrad yields less focused yet finely aligned gradients that closely follow image details. We attribute this to the Maxout activation retaining preactivation information, unlike ReLU, which discards it in inactive neurons.
